text:
Mika Zibanejad has 20 points in 24 games, which looks like business as usual for a center with 818 career points before this season. Look underneath and the engine is running a little differently. Last year he scored 34 goals; this year his own chance quality is down to 0.7 expected goals per 60 minutes, from 1.02. He's finishing at a normal rate (six goals on 5.7 expected), so nothing here is luck in either direction. He's just getting to fewer good spots.

The five-on-five picture is the worry. The Rangers take under 44% of shot attempts with him on the ice, and their share of expected goals (the quality of chances) is about even only because the shots against tend to be weaker. The power play, five points so far, still carries a lot of his value, as it did last season by Evolving-Hockey's count.

What to watch: whether the shot volume comes back. His shot is still one of the league's hardest (96th percentile on NHL EDGE), and our range has him around 71 points if his chance rate drifts toward normal.
headline: Zibanejad is producing on fewer chances
